thread.title: Why Investors In Apple, Technology Stocks Should Note U.S. Dollar Rise

author: REINHARDT KRAUSE
title: Why Investors In Apple, Technology Stocks Should Note U.S. Dollar Rise
text:
A rising U.S. dollar could soon be a negative for such technology stocks as Apple ( AAPL ), but the impact may not show up in the next round of earnings reports.
X If the U.S. dollar continues to rally over the summer, earnings for technology stocks could take a hit in the second half of the year.
The dollar "is now flat on a year-over-year basis, and is about to turn positive for the first time in roughly a year. If the strength continues, it may start to weigh on U.S. corporate earnings," economist Ed Yardeni said in a report published on Tuesday.
Akamai Technologies ( AKAM ) on Tuesday lowered revenue guidance citing the strengthening dollar. Akamai cut its June quarter sales forecast by $3 million to a range of $658 million to $663 million.
 Shares in software firm Red Hat ( RHT ) fell last week after its fiscal 2019 revenue outlook disappointed. Red Hat also cited currency exchange rates in its guidance.
Bank of America says June quarter earnings may not be impacted much.
"While the U.S. dollar strengthened over the course of the quarter, it is still weaker, on average, than in the year-ago quarter," the bank said in a report to clients.
Weak Dollar Boosted Earnings Technology stocks, including Apple, got a boost from a weak dollar in the March quarter and in late 2017.
"Multinationals saw more EPS and sales beats than domestically oriented companies in Q1. But with recent dollar strength and concerns over global growth and trade, this might not persist," said the Bank of America report.
Aside from impacting overseas earnings, a rising dollar also makes U.S. products more expensive.
Expectations that the Federal Reserve will continue hiking rates are one reason behind the dollar's rise. Goldman Sachs said in its note to clients that the U.S. dollar's rally may pause.
"Despite lingering risks from trade tensions, tighter emerging market financial conditions, and further weakness in ex-U.S. growth, we think the broad U.S. dollar seems most likely to depreciate in the second half" of 2018, the Goldman report said.
Apple shares climbed 1.2% to close at 184.43 on the stock market today . Akamai fell 2.5% to 75.72.
